title: Z-Score Standardization
statement: Implement `zscore(xs)` using the population standard deviation (divide variance by n, not n − 1). Return (x − mean) / sd for each element. If the standard deviation is 0, return zeros.

approaches.name: Center then scale
approaches.explanation: Z-scores put features on a common scale without bounding them to 0..1.

editorial: A z-score asks how many population standard deviations a value sits from the mean. Linear models with L2 penalties need this: a feature measured in millimeters would otherwise dominate one measured in kilometers. This problem uses the population definition (divide by n), which is what most ML scalers compute on the training column they just saw. The unbiased sample variance divides by n − 1 and is a statistics-course default, not the usual feature-scaler default. Say which one you used.
